provenance: Later literature check for portfolio revision, not original course source history

sources.title: How much water does rice use?
sources.author: IRRI / Rice Today
sources.supports: Field water inputs include rainfall and irrigation; an Asian experimental average is about 2,500 L per kg of rough rice.
sources.limit: Not a current India-specific rate or a direct benchmark for an untested chamber. Measurement boundaries must match.

sources.title: Alternate Wetting and Drying
sources.author: IRRI
sources.supports: AWD is an existing soil-based field-water practice.
sources.limit: It does not establish aeroponic performance or guaranteed carbon-credit income.

sources.title: Rice yields and water use under alternate wetting and drying irrigation: A meta-analysis
sources.author: Carrijo, Lundy & Linquist
sources.supports: Mild AWD reduced total water input by 23.4% versus continuous flooding, without a significant yield reduction in most circumstances.
sources.limit: Severe drying carried yield risk. Results are conditional and belong to the published studies, not this project.

sources.title: Machine-learning-assisted comparative analysis of rice growth and yield formation in field and plant factory systems
sources.author: Yang et al.
sources.supports: Controlled-environment rice developed faster in the experiment, without a significant increase in final grain yield.
sources.limit: Resource-use and economic indicators were incomplete; it does not validate the proposed stacked system.

sources.title: Pertumbuhan dan Hasil Empat Genotipe Padi (Oryiza Satifa L.) pada Sistem Budidaya Integrasi Padi-Ikan Secara Aquaponik
sources.author: Suparmin et al.
sources.supports: Rice–fish cultivation was studied with and without additional NPK; some yield components benefited from supplementation.
sources.limit: Soil-filled pots and catfish differ from the proposed soil-free system. No proof of zero fertiliser, zero methane, or higher income.

sources.title: Cytogenetic, electrophoretic, and root studies of javanica rices, in Rice Genetics II
sources.author: Chang et al. / IRRI
sources.type: Rice research chapter; indexed passages checked
sources.supports: Aeroponic culture was used for comparative rice-root research.
sources.limit: Root measurements do not establish full-cycle commercial grain production. Indexed publisher passages were checked; full-PDF retrieval timed out.

sources.title: Hydroponics in physiological studies of trace element tolerance and accumulation in plants focussing on metallophytes and hyperaccumulator plants
sources.author: van der Ent et al.
sources.supports: Its aeroponics discussion identifies specialised equipment, high-pressure pumps, and mister-clogging disadvantages.
sources.limit: Not a rice-yield trial; it does not establish a crop-death timeframe or validate predictive alerts.

sources.title: The Futures Cone, use and history
sources.author: Joseph Voros
sources.supports: Future categories are nested; preferable is a normative judgement that can overlap categories.
sources.limit: Not a probability model or evidence that any project scenario will occur.
